findings.description: Direct inspection of all eleven V150 views shows the broad cloth ballooning from V149 is removed, but the neutral/front/back/side and arm-pose skirt reads as a plain, smooth A-line shell with no legible pleat rhythm. Side views show large faceted folds and a hard, uneven hem junction; the authored-panel skinning hypothesis does not yet preserve a convincing pleated garment appearance.

Crouch and sit views expose oversized hard-edged shorts/thigh-cover shells across the upper legs while the skirt lifts and falls away behind the thighs. Pose-matched upper-thigh coverage is still only 0.371 per side in crouch and 0.271 per side in sit for the overskirt; shorts cover 0.642 and 0.638 per side respectively. These are geometry diagnostics only and do not establish fit.

Angular triangular patches and abrupt surface transitions remain visible across the torso and waist/hip in front, three-quarter, side, neutral and arm-cross views. This independent surface-quality blocker persists.
The prone render shows the garment and limbs intersecting/overlapping into a compact pile around the pelvis and chest; silhouette and surface continuity are not acceptable in this required pose.

nextAction: Keep candidate REJECTED and prototype-only. V150 removes severe native-cloth ballooning by evaluating the authored six-panel overskirt through armature skinning, but the result loses visible pleat character and still has side faceting/hem irregularity. Keep this method as a diagnostic candidate only; next improve the authored panel geometry and targeted weights so pleats remain readable without returning to broad unconstrained cloth. Separately redesign the shorts/thigh-cover shell cut and coverage for crouch and sit, and correct torso/waist surface artifacts and prone intersections. Rebuild and directly review all eleven poses after changes. Fit, UV, materials, Shape Keys, Unity, VRChat, package and release remain independent unverified gates.
